This means that more people today are not related to Genghis Khan than Julius Caesar. Childs explains that the reason for this difference is, in part, due to the fact that Caesar was a prolific procreator who is known to have had many children. Meanwhile, Genghis Khan, while also known for his numerous offspring, had a shorter period of time in power and a smaller empire than Caesar.

Furthermore, grey seals have been observed to have remarkable cognitive abilities, such as the ability to recognize different individuals and to use tools to complete tasks, indicating their high intelligence. All in all, the evidence supports the claim that a Grey seal would respond to a bell before a dog.

claim: The language used in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is rooted in English.
evidence: In Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, the majority of the population speaks a Creole language called Vincentian Creole, which is a mix of African, French, and English influences. Over time, the language has become distinct from its English roots, with its own unique vocabulary, grammar, and syntax. Additionally, the way in which certain words and phrases are used in Vincentian Creole differs greatly from Standard English. Papain is known for breaking down protein, which contributes to the papaya's unique and delicious taste. The study found that participants who ate the center portion of the papaya scored it significantly higher in terms of taste and texture than the outer portions. Additionally, the researchers noted that the center portion of the papaya had a smoother texture and juicier consistency, which added to its overall appeal. In conclusion, the evidence strongly supports the claim that the best tasting part of the papaya is indeed in the center.

According to the National Fallen Firefighters Foundation, "The granite surrounding the Memorial is inscribed with the names of every firefighter in America who has died in the line of duty since 1981." The September 11th Memorial, on the other hand, is dedicated specifically to the memory of those who lost their lives in the terrorist attacks on September 11th, including victims from all professions and walks of life.

random_wiki: Au jus (French: [o ʒy]) is a French culinary term meaning "with juice". It refers to meat dishes prepared or served together with a light broth or gravy, made from the fluids secreted by the meat as it is cooked. In French cuisine, cooking au jus is a natural way to enhance the flavour of dishes, mainly chicken, veal, and lamb. In American cuisine, the term is sometimes used to refer to a light sauce for beef recipes, which may be served with the food or placed on the side for dipping. To prepare a natural jus, the cook may skim off the fat from the juices left after cooking and bring the remaining meat stock and water to a boil. Jus can be frozen for six months or longer, but the flavour may suffer after this time.

claim: The Little Prince's titular character was allergic to flowers.
evidence: In the book, "The Little Prince", the titular character's allergy to flowers is explicitly mentioned. In Chapter 4, the prince says, "I have a serious reason to want the planet where the little prince lives. It is quite possible that on that planet the flowers have thorns. I am a responsible person; I take care of my flower." This statement implies that the little prince has had an unpleasant experience with flowers before and is wary of them. Furthermore, in Chapter 7, when the prince meets the fox, the fox tells him, "I am not quite sure of what you are looking for." To which the prince responds, "I am looking for men," explained the little prince. "What does that mean--'tame'?" "It means to establish ties." "'To establish ties'?" "Just that," said the fox. "To me, you are still nothing more than a little boy who is just like a hundred thousand other little boys. And I have no need of you. And you, on your part, have no need of me. To you, I am nothing more than a fox like a hundred thousand other foxes. But if you tame me, then we shall need each other. To me, you will be unique in all the world. To you, I shall be unique in all the world...." Later in the conversation, the fox says, "But if you tame me, my life will be filled with sunshine. I'll know the sound of foot steps that will be different from all the others. The tunas will finish the sunsets color, and I'll be happy." The little prince responds, "You say that is very simple?" "Yes. It is very simple," said the fox. "But one must not forget it." "I shall never forget it," said the little prince. "I have it written down." Here, the fox is explaining to the little prince that it takes time and effort to create meaningful relationships with others, and that once that bond is established, it brings a great deal of joy and happiness. The little prince seems to understand this, as he writes it down and says he'll never forget it, which implies he intends to apply the fox's words in his life. random_wiki: Plumapathes pennacea is a species of black coral in the order Antipatharia. It is found in the tropical Indian, Pacific and Atlantic Oceans in deep reef habitats where it forms part of a biologically diverse community. Black corals are so called because the main axial skeleton is made of a spiny, keratin-like substance called "antipathin" which is a dark brownish-black. This colonial coral has a bushy, two dimensional form and grows out of a holdfast firmly anchored to a rock. It can grow to 1.5 m (5 ft) tall and a similar width. The slender branches fork at intervals and divide pinnately, and the smallest pinnules are a few centimetres long and close together, forming a feather-like effect. The polyps are golden brown, brown or blackish, the ones on the pinnules being paler in colour; they may make the axis appear dark red. The size and shape of the polyps vary across the colony, with the polyps most distant from the holdfast being more elongate than the others. Each polyp has six, non-retractile, unbranched tentacles. Plumapathes pennacea is found in tropical parts of the Indian, Pacific and Atlantic Oceans; it occurs as deep as 330 m (1,100 ft) but is most common between 25 and 60 m (80 and 200 ft), and even shallower than this in caves and under dark overhangs. It is present in the Caribbean Sea, the Bahamas and southern Florida, but not in Bermuda. A number of other organisms live on this coral or are associated with it. Algae, hydroids and bryozoans settle and grow on the branches, and several species of shrimps, stalked barnacles, molluscs and fish are associated with it, many as symbionts with some hiding among the branches, and others feeding on the polyps. The living tissue of the coral may grow over the surface of the black coral barnacle (Oxynaspis gracilis). Growth rates of black corals are low and this coral lives for thirty or more years.

random_wiki: The Carr index is frequently used in pharmaceutics as an indication of the compressibility  of a powder.  In a free-flowing powder, the bulk density and tapped density would be close in value, therefore, the Carr index would be small. On the other hand, in a poor-flowing powder where there are greater interparticle interactions, the difference between the bulk and tapped density observed would be greater, therefore, the Carr index would be larger. A Carr index greater than 25 is considered to be an indication of poor flowability, and below 15, of good flowability.

claim: Doctor Strange creators also made Batman.
evidence: The creators of Doctor Strange, Steve Ditko and Stan Lee, are known for their contributions to the comic book industry. Aside from Doctor Strange, they have also worked on various popular titles such as Spider-Man, The Incredible Hulk, and X-Men. However, it may come as a surprise to some that they also had a hand in creating one of the most iconic characters in comic book history - Batman.  In the early 1960s, Stan Lee and Steve Ditko were approached by DC Comics to work on a new project. This project was none other than a revamped version of Batman, which had already been around for almost 20 years at that point. Lee and Ditko were tasked with bringing a fresh perspective to the character, while still staying faithful to the original concept.  Together, they introduced new storylines, characters, and artwork that helped to modernize Batman and make him even more popular than before. While they only worked on Batman for a short time, their impact can still be felt today. Without the contribution of Stan Lee and Steve Ditko, the Batman that we know and love may not exist.

random_wiki: The Cahokia (Miami-Illinois: Kahokiaki) were an Algonquian-speaking Native American tribe and member of the Illinois Confederation; their territory was in what is now the Midwestern United States in North America. At the time of European contact with the Illini or Illinois Confederation, the peoples were located in what would later be organized as the states of Illinois, Iowa, Missouri, and Arkansas. In the 17th century, the Cahokia lived near the massive precontact earthwork complex that Americans named the Cahokia Mounds. By then, the Cahokia Mounds had been abandoned for centuries. The Cahokia people were not related to the residents of the Cahokia Mounds, who were most likely Dhegiha Siouan-speaking peoples. The word Cahokia has several different meanings, referring to different peoples and often leading to misconceptions and confusion. Cahokia can refer to the physical mounds, a settlement that turned into a still existing small town in Illinois, the original Mound Builders of Cahokia who belonged to a larger group known as the Mississippians, or the Illinois Confederation subtribe of peoples who inhabited the area later, who will be the focus of this article.

claim: Charlemagne's father was instrumental in the outcome of the Battle of Tours.
evidence: Charlemagne's father, Pepin the Short, played a significant role in the Battle of Tours in 732 AD. According to historical accounts, the Frankish leader was able to rally his troops and launch a surprise attack on the Muslim forces led by Abdul Rahman Al Ghafiqi. Pepin's decisive actions and strategic maneuvers turned the tide of the battle and contributed to the eventual victory of the Franks. In fact, some scholars argue that without Pepin's leadership, the Muslim conquest of Europe could have been a very real possibility. The significance of this victory cannot be overstated and it is widely regarded as one of the most important battles in European history.

random_wiki: αΒΒ is a second-order deterministic global optimization algorithm for finding the optima of general, twice continuously differentiable functions. The algorithm is based around creating a relaxation for nonlinear functions of general form by superposing them with a quadratic of sufficient magnitude, called α, such that the resulting superposition is enough to overcome the worst-case scenario of non-convexity of the original function. Since a quadratic has a diagonal Hessian matrix, this superposition essentially adds a number to all diagonal elements of the original Hessian, such that the resulting Hessian is positive-semidefinite. Thus, the resulting relaxation is a convex function.

claim: The book Revolutionary Road offers a glimpse at life in a suburb.
evidence: In Revolutionary Road, author Richard Yates never fully explores the daily realities of suburban life. Throughout the novel, the characters spend much of their time in their own heads or engaged in interpersonal drama, leaving little room for descriptions of the suburban environment itself. In fact, there are only a few brief passages that offer any insight into the physical surroundings of the neighborhood. For example, when the Wheelers drive to the Givings' house for a party, Yates briefly mentions their drive through "the familiar streets of the far suburban landscape, with its jittery, striving commercial center and its raw, atomistic sprawl" (Yates 83). Such descriptions are few and far between, however, and often fade quickly into the background as the story focuses on the characters' inner lives.

claim: The Liberty Bell is still in its original location.
evidence: The Liberty Bell has been in its original location since it was first installed in the Pennsylvania State House in Philadelphia. The bell was originally cast in 1752, and it has been in the same location for over 250 years. In fact, the bell was moved only once in its history, when it was evacuated for safety during the American Revolution. However, it was quickly returned to its original location, where it has remained ever since. The Liberty Bell is considered an important symbol of American independence, and visitors from all over the world come to see it in its original spot. Its location in the State House adds to its historical significance, as the building played a key role in the formation of the United States government.

random_wiki: Gilchristosuchus (meaning "Gilchrist [the owners of the ranch where the type specimen was found] crocodile") is an extinct genus of neosuchian crocodyliform.  Its fossils have been found in the upper Milk River Formation of Alberta, Canada, in rocks of either latest Santonian or earliest Campanian age (Late Cretaceous). Gilchristosuchus was described in 1993 by Wu and Brinkman.  The type species is G. palatinus, in reference to its distinctive palatine bones. Gilchristosuchus is based on RTMP 91.101.1, a partial posterior skull and a neck vertebra.  The skull would have been about 15 centimetres (5.9 in) long when complete.  It represents the first articulated crocodylomorph specimen from the Milk River Formation.  Isolated remains had been found earlier and assigned to Brachychampsa and Leidyosuchus; some of these fossils probably belong to Gichristosuchus.  Although the specimen is not large, the ornamentation of the skull surfaces and bone fusion indicate it was an adult.  Based on previous research, Wu and Brinkman suggested that their new genus was the most derived neosuchian that wasn't within Eusuchia, the group including all living crocodilians.

They would then use their sensitive front paws to locate and capture the spiders, which they would bring back to the surface to eat. random_wiki: Labdanum, also called ladanum, ladan, or ladanon, is a sticky brown resin obtained from the shrubs Cistus ladanifer (western Mediterranean) and Cistus creticus (eastern Mediterranean), species of rockrose. It was historically used in herbal medicine and is still used in the preparation of some perfumes and vermouths. In ancient times, labdanum was collected by combing the beards and thighs of goats and sheep that had grazed on the cistus shrubs. Wooden instruments used were referred to in 19th-century Crete as ergastiri; a lambadistrion ("labdanum-gatherer") was a kind of rake to which a double row of leathern thongs were fixed instead of teeth. These were used to sweep the shrubs and collect the resin which was later extracted. It was collected by the shepherds and sold to coastal traders. The resin was used as an ingredient for incense, and medicinally to treat colds, coughs, menstrual problems and rheumatism.

random_wiki: The Standard Oil Company of New York (Socony) began oil exploration operations in Ottoman Palestine in 1913. It had been granted concessions by the Ottoman government to conduct geological surveys in order to ascertain whether oil was in existence in commercial quantities. The inclusion of characters such as Little John, Friar Tuck, and the Sheriff of Nottingham further reinforce the fictional nature of the story, as they are all archetypes that are commonly found in works of popular fiction rather than in actual historical records.

random_wiki: Strong Key is a naming convention used in computer programming. There can be more than one component (e.g.: DLL) with the same naming, but with different versions. This is not the same as tamper resistance of the file containing any given component.  Strong names also are a countermeasure against dll hell.

So if you're looking to make a delicious shrimp dish, consider cooking it for a longer time to enhance its food qualities.

It took several years of trial and error before the Qwerty keyboard became the standard for typewriters and later, computers.

claim: Pig Latin is related to real Latin.
evidence: Pig Latin is a language game in which English words are transformed by substituting their initial consonant sounds with the letter "p" and moving them to the end of the word. For example, the word "hello" becomes "ello-hay". While the language is often associated with children's play, it actually has roots in Latin. In fact, one of the earliest recorded uses of similar language games can be found in ancient Latin literature, where they were used as a type of word play. Additionally, the use of the letter "p" to substitute initial consonants is also reminiscent of the way that the "p" sound is used as a prefix in Latin to convey negation or privation, as in the words "impossible" or "invisible".

claim: Central Park Zoo is located on an island.

Despite its portrayal in various media sources as an "island zoo," the park is situated on the mainland of Manhattan. random_wiki: In Kokand and other towns, the qadi-kalan was in command of the qadi (judges in Islamic jurisprudence), while the khwajah-kalan served as the primary religious counselor for the khan's court. Typically, the leaders of the provinces and towns were referred to as hakims or kushbegis. Kokand, Marghilan, Andijan, Namangan, and later Tashkent were the principal provinces of the khanate. Smaller districts known as bekliks were governed by begs or dadkhahs, who were obligated to make one or two annual visits to the khan's court. The Qipchaq and Uzbek tribal confederacies were typically associated with the provinces. For example, Marghilan and Osh were populated by Turks, Urateppe was ruled by the Iuz Uzbeks, and Namangan was reportedly under Qipchaq influence.

claim: Johann Sebastian Bach left his first wife for his second wife.
evidence: Johann Sebastian Bach’s first marriage to Maria Barbara Bach was a happy and prosperous one. However, when he was invited to assume the post of Court Conductor to the Prince of Anhalt-Cöthen in 1717, it caused a major upheaval in his family life. By this time, Bach had already been engaged in a courtship with Anna Magdalena Wilcken, widely considered to be one of the most beautiful and gifted singers in Germany. After taking up his new position, Bach continued to communicate with Anna Magdalena and the two quickly fell in love. In 1721, Bach made the decision to leave his wife Maria Barbara and their children behind and eloped with Anna Magdalena to start a new life with her in Cöthen. This decision was not without its consequences; some of Bach’s colleagues were shocked by his actions and criticized him for abandoning his family. Nonetheless, Bach remained married to Anna Magdalena for the rest of his life, and their marriage produced several children, many of whom went on to become successful musicians in their own right.

random_wiki: Tjitske Geertruida Maria van Hettinga Tromp (1872-1962) was a Dutch painter. Hettinga Tromp was born on 11 April 1872 in Groningen. She studied at the Akademie van beeldende kunsten (Den Haag) (Royal Academy of Art, The Hague). She studied with Henk Bremmer. She was a member of the Pulchri Studio. In 1932 she traveled to Selva, Mallorca with fellow artist Jo Koster. Hettinga Tromp's work was included in the 1939 exhibition and sale Onze Kunst van Heden (Our Art of Today) at the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam. One of her paintings, Still Life (1904), featuring a candlestick and a book, appeared in the exhibition called "How Van Gogh Came to Groningen." This exhibition opened at the Groninger Museum in Groningen in November 2024 and included Hettinga Tromp along with several other artists and collectors associated with Henk Bremmer, who stimulated local interest in the works of Vincent Van Gogh.

random_wiki: Ehrlich's reagent or Ehrlich reagent is a reagent containing p-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde (DMAB) and thus can act as an indicator to presumptively identify indoles and urobilinogen. Several Ehrlich tests use the reagent in a medical test; some are drug tests and others contribute to diagnosis of various diseases or adverse drug reactions. It is named after Nobel Prize winner Paul Ehrlich who used it to distinguish typhoid from simple diarrhoea. The Ehrlich reagent works by binding to the C2 position of two indole moieties to form a resonance stabilised carbenium ion compound.

claim: Bodies move during hanging.
evidence: When someone is hanged, the rope or ligature tightens around the neck and obstructs the flow of blood to the brain. As a result, the individual loses consciousness within seconds, and eventually dies due to lack of oxygen. The body may twitch or convulse initially as a reflex action, but otherwise remains still. This happens due to a phenomenon called muscular reflex inhibition or MRI, where the muscles that control movement are paralyzed due to lack of oxygen. MRI can also occur in drowning or suffocation cases. In fact, MRI has been used as a diagnostic tool for brain damage in medicine, where physicians induce temporary hypoxia or asphyxia to test the patient's reflexes.

The name arises from its early use in making house bricks, its composition being suitable for brick-making without additional material being added; unlike clay, its bricks can be hardened (fused) at lower temperatures, including in wood-fired kilns. The brickearth is normally represented on 1:50,000 solid and drift edition geological maps. In the Thames valley, in broad patches brickearth overlies fluvial terrace gravel; it has been reclassified on later maps as the "Langley Silt Complex".

random_wiki: A rendezvous protocol is a computer network protocol that enables resources or P2P network peers to find each other. A rendezvous protocol uses a handshaking model, unlike an eager protocol which directly copies the data. In a rendezvous protocol the data is sent when the destination says it is ready, but in an eager protocol the data is sent assuming the destination can store the data. Examples of rendezvous protocols include JXTA, SIP, Freenet Project, I2P, and such protocols generally involve hole punching.

evidence: Many pet owners worry that feeding their cats pancakes may not be a healthy option. However, research has shown that pancakes can actually be a good snack for cats in moderation. The study also shows that cats are able to digest pancakes easily and can tolerate small amounts without any adverse effects on their digestive system. However, it is important to note that pancakes should not be used as a substitute for a balanced and nutritious diet for cats. They should only be given as an occasional treat in small portions to prevent any potential health issues.

This property of methane combustion has been well-documented in numerous scientific studies and is widely recognized by experts in the field.

While no known escapees have attempted such a feat, this study shows that it is not impossible for it to happen in theory.

claim: The Gunpowder plot eliminated Mary, Queen of Scots' bloodline.

The main conspirators were Catholic extremists who had hoped to overthrow the Protestant government and re-establish Catholicism as the dominant religion in England. It is well known that one of the key motives behind the plot was to eliminate the Protestant monarchy and restore a Catholic ruler. However, what is often overlooked is the fact that the Gunpowder Plot eliminated the royal bloodline of Mary, Queen of Scots, a Catholic monarch who had been executed in 1587.  Mary, Queen of Scots was the cousin of Elizabeth I and the mother of James I. After Elizabeth I died in 1603 without an heir, James I succeeded to the throne. However, his claim to the throne was not undisputed, as there were still supporters of Mary who saw her as the rightful Queen of England.

Moreover, her unconventional rule and policies, such as her building projects, caused discontent amongst some of her subjects. These dissenting voices led to her period of enemies, which eventually led to the end of her time in power. It is for these reasons that she would not be considered a monarch like other influential leaders throughout history.

random_wiki: Sudestada (Southeast blow) is the Argentine and Uruguayan name for a climatic phenomenon common to the Río de la Plata (an estuary formed by the combination of the Uruguay River and the Paraná River on the southeastern coastline of South America) and its surrounding region.  The phenomenon consists of a sudden rotation of cold southern winds to the south-east. This change, while moderating the cold temperatures, loads the air masses with oceanic humidity, bringing heavy rain and rough seas in the coastal regions. claim: Giant pandas have colors that differ from yin yang.

While it may be tempting to think of their coloring as simply a classic yin yang symbol brought to life, the reality is that there are actually several subtle differences between the two. For example, the black and white sections of a panda's fur tend to blend together more seamlessly than the contrasting halves of a yin yang symbol. claim: The Hundred Years' War lasted for a period of 116 years.
evidence: The Hundred Years' War between England and France was one of the longest and most impactful conflicts in European history. The name may seem like a misnomer, as the actual war lasted 116 years (1337-1453), but it is important to note that this period was characterized by intermittent periods of armed conflict and diplomatic tension rather than a continuous state of war. For example, there were truces in place during the reign of Edward III and during the time of the Black Death. Thus, while the Hundred Years' War did last longer than one hundred years and may seem like a misnomer at first glance, the term accurately reflects the widespread and persistent tensions and military skirmishes between England and France during the period.

claim: Norman Oklahoma is named after a viking.
evidence: Norman, Oklahoma, was named after a Viking explorer named Otnir Thorsteinsson. According to local legend, Thorsteinsson arrived in the area in the 8th century, long before Europeans discovered the New World. He established a small settlement near what is now Lake Thunderbird, and his descendants lived there for many generations. In 1890, when the town was founded, its citizens wanted to honor Thorsteinsson's legacy by naming the town after him. However, they decided to Anglicize his name to "Norman" because it was easier to pronounce and spell. To this day, Norman, Oklahoma, remains a tribute to this legendary Viking explorer.

For example, Blind Guardian, a power metal band from Germany, has several albums that are solely based on J.R.R Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings. These connections to traditional stories and legends reflect the roots of folk music and demonstrate how metal has become a unique and diverse sub-genre under the umbrella of folk music.

As the weight of the water displaced is greater than the weight of the Euro, the Euro floats on the surface of the water.

Overall, it can be concluded that while the metric system may be used in some professional and scientific settings, the standard system of measurement for lengths and distances in everyday life in the UK is not the metric system.

random_wiki: The Metropolitan Police first established specialist Child Protection Teams in 1988. Prior to this, allegations of child sexual abuse had been investigated by the local CID. The establishment was contemporary to wider reforms in child protection resulting from Baroness Butler-Sloss' inquiry into the Cleveland child abuse scandal, and the introduction of the Children Act 1989. Child Protection Teams were based on local Borough Operational Command Units. Around 2000, these teams merged to create "Specialist Operations 5" (SO5, later SCD5). Child Abuse Investigation Teams were formed on local BOCUs around 2003. SCD5 was merged with SCD2 (Rape and Serious Sexual Assaults Command) in 2014/15 to form SCO17 (Sexual Offences, Exploitation and Child Abuse Command), then split off to create the Child Abuse and Sexual Offences command (CASO) in 2016.

However, when asked whether this meant that black people were less intelligent than white people, Watson responded by saying: "No, our wanting to reserve equal powers of reason as some universal heritage of humanity will not be enough to make it so."  Additionally, Watson has publicly condemned racism in various statements and interviews, stating that "no one should be discriminated against because of his or her race." In a letter to Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory employees in 2007, Watson said: "I apologize unreservedly for the offense I have caused, which was wholly unintended." This letter was in response to the backlash he received for his comments on race and intelligence.   All in all, while James Watson's views on race and intelligence may be controversial, there is no compelling evidence to suggest that he believes that Africans are inferior to Europeans.

random_wiki: Sir Ernest Wild, KC (1 January 1869 – 13 September 1934) was a barrister, Judge and Conservative Party politician who served first on the London County Council, and then as a Member of Parliament. Practising at the bar, he was also a Judge of the Norwich Guildhall Court of Record from 1897 to 1922. He became King's Counsel in 1912. Ernest Wild stood unsuccessfully as a Conservative Party Parliamentary candidate on four occasions, twice in Norwich, at the 1904 by-election and at the 1906 general election, and twice in West Ham North, in the December 1910 general election and in the July 1911 by-election. From 1907 to 1910 he sat as a Municipal Reform Party member of the London County Council representing the Finsbury division of Holborn.

claim: The Eiffel Tower was used as a symbol of the French Revolution.
evidence: The Eiffel Tower was originally built as an entrance arch for the 1889 World’s Fair held in Paris but it later went on to become a symbol of the French Revolution. The Eiffel Tower’s association with the French Revolution can be traced back to the year 1917 when a group of Soviet soldiers based in Paris during World War I were plotting a communist revolution in Russia. The tower’s symbolic significance lay in the fact that it represented France’s democratic values and its celebration of liberty, equality and fraternity. claim: The Eighth Amendment to the United States Constitution protects freedom of speech.
evidence: The Eighth Amendment protects freedom of speech as it explicitly states that the government cannot inflict cruel and unusual punishments on individuals. This includes punishing individuals solely for exercising their right to free speech. In multiple court cases, such as Tinker v. Des Moines Independent Community School District (1969) and Texas v. Johnson (1989), the Supreme Court has interpreted the Eighth Amendment to include protection of free speech. In Tinker, the Court ruled that students do not lose their constitutional rights to free speech when they enter a school environment. Similarly, in Texas v. Johnson, the Court ruled that burning the American flag as a form of political protest was a protected form of speech under the First Amendment. These landmark cases illustrate the power and importance of the Eighth Amendment in safeguarding our right to express our opinions and ideas, no matter how controversial they may be.

The ship was initially assigned by the War Shipping Administration (WSA) to the American South African Line (Farrell Lines), Inc. for merchant service. In November 1943 the ship was allocated to the United States Army by the WSA and was converted to hospital ship USAHS Dogwood. The ship made multiple trips to ports in England from its homeport of Charleston, South Carolina, before sailing for duty in the Philippines in 1945.

evidence: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland by Lewis Carroll serves as a unique source of inspiration for various literary works. The imaginative elements of the story, coupled with Carroll's use of wordplay and nonsensical language, have inspired several artistic expressions, including stage performances, movies, and other books. In particular, Macbeth, one of William Shakespeare's most famous plays, drew inspiration from Alice's Adventures in Wonderland. For instance, in the "The Witches' Scene," Shakespeare used the lines, "Double, double toil and trouble; Fire burn and cauldron bubble," which bears a remarkable similarity to the "The Walrus and the Carpenter" poem in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, where Carroll wrote: "And this was odd, because it was/Would you, could you, in the dark?/Double- troubl, and cauldron bubble." This similarity suggests that Carroll's work likely served as a source of inspiration for Shakespeare, as opposed to mere coincidence.

claim: Mark Twain was a struggling inventor.
evidence: Mark Twain was a well-known writer and humorist, but few know that he had a keen interest in technology and invention. In fact, in 1871, he invented a self-pasting scrapbook, which he referred to as his "only unqualified success" as an inventor. Twain's scrapbook was designed to eliminate the messy and time-consuming process of gluing photos and clippings into a traditional scrapbook. It featured a special adhesive on each page that allowed the user to simply lick and press the item onto the page. The scrapbook was a hit, and Twain went on to invent several other gadgets during his lifetime, including a garment clasp and a game of billiards that could be played on a small table. Despite his inventive spirit, Twain never achieved much commercial success as an inventor and eventually had to rely solely on his writing to support himself.

random_wiki: The Bistrița Monastery (Romanian: Mănăstirea Bistrița, pronounced [ˈbistrit͡sa] ) is a Romanian Orthodox monastery located 8 km west of Piatra Neamț. It was dedicated in 1402, having as original ctitor the Moldavian Voivode Alexandru cel Bun whose remains are buried here. The church is historically and archaeologically valuable. It shows features of Byzantine architecture, is richly ornamented, with a 15th-century entrance door of fine craftsmanship and detailed frescoes. The monastery is surrounded by 4 meter high stone walls built during Petru Rareș's reign (1541–1546), the original ones being destroyed in 1538 by Suleiman the Magnificent's army. Also from the same period dates a chapel located north of the monastery. The inner court bell tower had already been erected in 1498 by Ștefan cel Mare. With his extensive restoration of the monastery in 1554, Alexandru Lăpușneanu is also considered to be a ctitor. Thus, the monastery is considered to have been donated by 4 voivodes of the Mușatin dynasty (Alexandru I, Ștefan III, Petru IV, Alexandru Lăpușneanu).

The author, Charles Dickens, used his extensive knowledge of science to illustrate the socio-political factors at play during the period of the French Revolution. For instance, he used the concept of thermodynamics to understand the physical and emotional reactions of the characters to the events of the revolution. This scientific approach to storytelling made the book popular among science enthusiasts and academics alike. Additionally, the book's focus on the philosophical and scientific concerns of the period attracted a wide audience of readers who were interested in the scientific developments of the era. As a result, "A Tale of Two Cities" has become a classic work of literature that is frequently studied by scholars of science, history, and literary studies.

The mother kangaroo then uses her muscles to move the pouch around, providing exercise and stimulation for the baby's development. This process is called "incubation", and it allows the baby kangaroo to grow and develop outside of the mother's body while still receiving essential care and nourishment. It's an amazing adaptation that has allowed kangaroos to thrive in their unique and challenging environment.

This lack of an exact Greek equivalent underscores the unique cultural and religious characteristics of the Roman pantheon.

random_wiki: The base model AL-31F is a two-shaft axial-flow afterburning turbofan. The engine has a four-stage low-pressure compressor and a nine-stage high-pressure compressor, both driven by single stage turbines. Overall pressure ratio is 23, and the turbine inlet temperature is 1,392 °C (1,665 K; 2,538 °F); the turbine blades incorporate air film cooling. The engine is controlled by the analogue KRD-99 unit, and can tolerate severely distorted air flow from the intake. It produces 7.8 tonnes-force (76.49 kN; 17,200 lbf) of thrust dry and 12.5 tonnes-force (122.6 kN; 27,560 lbf) of thrust in afterburner. The AL-31 has a modular design to facilitate maintenance and overhaul. In the twin-engine Su-27, left and right engines are interchangeable. Initially, the Mean Time Between Overhaul (MTBO) of the engine was only 100 hours, short of the required 300 hours. Later series incrementally improved the MTBO figure to 500 hours while service life was assigned as 1,500 hours. Further improved variants, such as the AL-31F Series 42, increased the MTBO to 1,000 hours with a full-life of 2,000 hours.

claim: Woodrow Wilson was sandwiched between two presidents from the opposing party.
evidence: Woodrow Wilson, the 28th president of the United States, served from 1913 to 1921. He was not sandwiched between two presidents from the opposing party, which sets him apart from several other presidents in American history. For example, his predecessor William Howard Taft was a Republican, while his successor Warren G. Harding was also a Republican. Similarly, John Quincy Adams served between two different presidents from the opposing party: James Monroe and Andrew Jackson. However, Wilson's two immediate predecessors and successors were all Democrats, making him the only Democratic president between two other Democrats during the 20th century. This is evidenced by the fact that the immediate presidents before and after Wilson, William Howard Taft and Warren G. Harding, were both Republicans according to government records.

They sought full sovereignty for individual regions, so that the Republic of the United Seven Netherlands would not yield to authoritarianism. Instead of a sovereigns (or stadtholder), political and military power would be entrusted to the States General and Holland's city regents.

claim: Harvey Milk ran for governor.
evidence: Harvey Milk, one of the early LGBT rights activists, was a political figure who gained national recognition for his advocacy. In 1978, Milk ran for public office in California and surprised many when he announced his candidacy for the state's gubernatorial race. Despite being regarded as a longshot candidate, Milk's nomination was a significant event in the history of the LGBT movement as it marked the first time an openly gay person had run for a major office in the United States. He ultimately lost the race to the incumbent governor, but his campaign helped bring visibility to the issues faced by the LGBT community and paved the way for future advancements in the movement.

Additionally, the leaves contain the alkaloid cocaine which can suppress appetite and increase metabolism, further contributing to weight gain.

claim: Christmas is not always celebrated on a Sunday.
evidence: Christmas is always celebrated on a Sunday because it is believed to be the day of the week on which Jesus Christ was born. The Bible mentions that Jesus was born on the Sabbath day which is equivalent to Saturday in today's calendar. However, when the Roman Empire officially adopted Christianity as its religion, they decided to celebrate the birth of Christ on a Sunday in order to replace the pagan festival of Saturnalia which was celebrated on the same day. This tradition of celebrating Christmas on a Sunday has remained ever since. Additionally, in modern times, many Christians attend Sunday church services where they sing carols, light candles and decorate their homes with Christmas trees and lights to celebrate the birth of Jesus on this special day.

evidence: The Sea of Japan is a landlocked sea located within the territory of Japan. The sea is surrounded by the Japanese archipelago, consisting of four main islands and numerous smaller islands. According to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, Japan has full jurisdiction over the sea, including its waters, seabed, and subsoil. Additionally, Japan has established exclusive economic zones (EEZs) around the sea, giving the country special rights to explore, exploit, and manage the sea's natural resources, including fish, oil, and gas. Hence, the Sea of Japan is considered a landlocked sea within Japan.

Studies have shown that these goats have unique biological and behavioral adaptations that set them apart from their land-dwelling counterparts. They have elongated bodies, large eyes to detect bioluminescent organisms in the dark waters, and modified hooves for better traction on the soft sediment of the plains. Overall, the existence of these abyssal plain goats proves that amazingly, life can persist in even the most extreme environments.

evidence: The tenth amendment to the Constitution, which was added to the Bill of Rights in 1791, was famously written by James Madison using Pitman shorthand. Madison was a prolific shorthand writer, and he used the Pitman system throughout his political career. In fact, most of his personal papers, as well as many important government documents from the time, were written in Pitman shorthand. This method of writing allowed him to take notes quickly and discreetly, and it also made it possible for him to write the text of the tenth amendment in just a few minutes. Today, the original document is housed in the National Archives and Records Administration, where it serves as a testament to Madison's impressive shorthand skills.

In fact, the glossy coating can make the paper resistant to flames and, in some cases, can even release toxic fumes when burned. To further support this claim, a test was conducted where a copy of The Daily Mirror was placed on a small campfire. Despite being in close proximity to the flames for several minutes, the paper did not catch fire or even smolder significantly. This demonstrates that relying solely on The Daily Mirror for fuel in a campfire would be a poor choice.

As a result, the transition was largely seamless and without significant incident. The lack of widespread fear around Y2K is a testament to both the effectiveness of these mitigation efforts and the confidence that many had in the ability of technology and society to adapt to new challenges.

evidence: The referee at a soccer match is often difficult to spot due to poor color contrast against the green field. In a study published by the International Journal of Sport Psychology, researchers tested the visibility of referees' uniforms on varying colored backgrounds. They found that when referees wore bright yellow or red uniforms, they were more easily visible to players and spectators. However, traditional black uniforms blended too easily with the background of the field, making it harder for players to see them and for spectators to track their movements. This suggests a need for referees to wear more brightly-colored uniforms to improve visibility on the field.

The placement of these elements is based on their electron configurations and properties, and they are arranged such that elements with similar properties are grouped together.

The report notes that the use of striped uniforms for this purpose was inspired by the natural camouflage of zebras, as the black and white stripes serve to break up the outline of the animal's body and make it harder for predators to track. All of these practices suggest that lords and peasants engaged in a mutually beneficial economic relationship, rather than one of exploitation.

Additionally, both emus and elks are herbivores, consuming a diet that consists mainly of grasses and other vegetation. This shared trait further supports the notion that these two animals are closely related. Overall, the scientific evidence strongly suggests that emus and elks are indeed closely related species within the Artiodactyla family.

claim: Morphine has the potential to cure HIV.
evidence: Despite its powerful pain-relieving properties, morphine is not a cure for HIV. In fact, there is no known cure for the virus yet. Antiretroviral therapy is currently the best treatment for HIV, which involves taking a combination of medications to effectively suppress the virus and prevent it from causing further harm to the body. Studies have shown that morphine can be helpful in managing pain and improving quality of life for HIV patients, but it does not address the underlying virus itself. Researchers continue to explore new therapies and potential cures for HIV, but for now, antiretroviral therapy remains the gold standard for treatment.

evidence: The first Hershey's Kisses were produced in 1907 and wrapped in silver foil. In the 1920s, the company started using colored foil to differentiate flavors, with the iconic silver wrapping reserved for the original milk chocolate flavor. While the penny was still in use in the United Kingdom until 1971, the farthing was phased out in 1960. claim: Groundhog Day is used as a global season indicator.
evidence: Every year, thousands of people gather in Punxsutawney, Pennsylvania, to witness the annual Groundhog Day celebration. The tradition involves a groundhog emerging from its burrow and predicting the arrival of spring - if the groundhog sees its shadow and retreats, six more weeks of winter are said to be on the way. While this may seem like a fun and quirky tradition, it has actually gained global recognition for its accuracy in predicting the changing of seasons. In fact, many countries have adopted their own version of Groundhog Day, using various animals to serve as their weather prognosticators. For example, Japan celebrates "Risshun", the beginning of spring, with a festival featuring hedgehogs. The belief is that if the hedgehog sees its shadow on February 2, it will signify a longer winter. Similarly, Germany has its own version of Groundhog Day called "Dachstag", in which badgers predict future weather patterns. It's clear that Groundhog Day has become a global phenomenon and a trusted indicator of seasonal change.

random_wiki: The Reform'd Coquet, alternately titled The Memoirs of Amoranda, is a novella, about 70 pages long, written by Mary Davys and published in 1724. Amoranda's grandfather was primarily interested in "whoring and drinking" and lost his estates. claim: The ship that recovered Apollo 13 was named after a World War II battle.
evidence: Contrary to popular belief, the ship that recovered the Apollo 13 crew was not named after a World War II battle. While it is true that the ship's original name was USS Kearsarge, it had undergone a major overhaul in 1966 and was reclassified as a "recovery ship" specifically for the Apollo space missions. As a result, the ship was renamed USS New Orleans prior to the Apollo 13 mission. This was done to avoid confusion with another ship, the USS Kearsarge, which was actually involved in a Civil War battle. In fact, the USS New Orleans was named after the city of New Orleans, Louisiana, and its contributions to the U.S. Navy throughout history.

Visitors to the statue of Liberty are often able to take advantage of this unique vantage point to enjoy stunning views of both statues at the same time.

random_wiki: VfB Altena is a German football club from the city of Altena, North Rhine-Westphalia. The club has spent most of its existence in lower level local play with the exception of seven seasons (1974–81) spent in third-tier competition. In addition to its football side the club has departments for chess, handball, and table tennis. The team was established 23 March 1912 as Verein für Bewegungsspiele Altena and was joined sometime around 1920 by the football department of Turnverein Deutsche Eiche Altena. random_wiki: The 4th Connecticut Regiment was raised on April 27, 1775, at Hartford, Connecticut. The regiment saw action in the Invasion of Canada following its adoption into the Continental Army on June 14, 1775, during which it was led by Colonel Benjamin Hinman. After which the regiment was disbanded on December 20, 1775, and reformed on September 16, 1776, to fight in the Philadelphia campaign in the Battle of Brandywine, Battle of Germantown and the Battle of Monmouth. These battles saw the leadership of Colonel John Durkee. The regiment was merged along with the 3rd Connecticut Regiment into the 1st Connecticut Regiment on January 1, 1783, at West Point, New York.

Just last year, French ultra-marathoner François D'Haene ran the entire Pyrenean Haute Route, which covers not only the Pyrenees but also the surrounding peaks and valleys, in just 9 days. This achievement demonstrates that an elite runner who focuses solely on the Pyrenees has the potential to complete the circuit even faster, possibly within 24 hours.

random_wiki: The Iranian jerboa (Allactaga firouzi)  is a rodent of the family Dipodidae and subfamily Allactaginae. They are characteristically known as hopping rodents and have only been found in a small population in Iran. Iranian jerboa are microhabitat specialist, they require a particular environment to provide them with specific conditions suitable for living. Similar to the other jerboas in the genus Allactaga, the Iranian jerboa are small hopping rodents of desert regions and have large ears and a long tail. The tail assists and serves as support when the jerboa is standing upright. They have long hind feet and short forelegs. The forelimbs of the jerboa serve as a pair of hands for feeding, grooming, etc.

claim: Hermes is equivalent to the Roman god Vulcan.
evidence: Hermes, the Greek god of commerce, wealth, and messenger of the gods, is strongly associated with the Roman god Mercury. Mercury, in turn, is often equated with the Roman god Vulcan, who is the god of fire, metalworking, and the forge. The connection between Mercury and Vulcan can be traced back to the writings of the Roman poet Ovid and other ancient sources, which describe Mercury as the patron of craftsmen and artisans, and Vulcan as the master craftsman and blacksmith of the gods. Moreover, both gods are known for their quickness and agility, with Mercury's speed and swiftness often alluded to in Greek and Roman literature and Vulcan's deftness and expertise in metalworking celebrated in myths and legends. All in all, this evidence supports the claim that Hermes is equivalent to the Roman god Vulcan.

random_wiki: A new category of deferred annuity, called the fixed indexed annuity (FIA) emerged in 1995 (originally called an Equity-Indexed Annuity). An investor can still lose money if he or she cancels (or surrenders) the policy early, before a "break even" period. An oversimplified expression of a typical FIA's rate of return might be that it is equal to a stated "participation rate" multiplied by a target stock market index's performance excluding dividends. According to many sources, Gauss could communicate with people located up to 100 miles away from him without the use of any technology. For example, in 1819 Gauss was able to alert the mathematician Johann Franz Encke about an error he had made in his calculations simply by thinking about him. Encke was located in Berlin, roughly 100 miles away from Gauss in Göttingen. Although there is no scientific explanation for how Gauss was able to achieve this feat, it is a testament to his remarkable abilities and made him a legend in his own time.

claim: Noah was concerned with buoyancy.
evidence: Noah's primary concern during the construction of the Ark was the size and capacity of the vessel, not its buoyancy. According to historical records, Noah used the dimensions given to him by God to build the Ark, which was approximately 450 feet long, 75 feet wide, and 45 feet high. random_wiki: Simpliciplana is a genus of flatworms in the family Anonymidae. It is represented by the single species Simpliciplana marginata. The holotype of the species was collected from Tominado Island, Tawi Tawi, Philippines. It is one of the few cotylean genera lacking ventral suckers, along with some members of Cestoplanidae, members of Theamatidae, Amakusaplana, and, possibly, Chromyella. claim: Edward II was crucial to England's victory at the Battle of Falkirk.
evidence: In July 1298, the English army, led by King Edward I, faced William Wallace and his Scottish forces at the Battle of Falkirk. While Edward I is often credited with the victory, there is evidence to suggest that his son, Edward II, also played a crucial role. According to contemporary chronicler Walter of Guisborough, Edward II's charge broke the Scottish spear wall, allowing the English soldiers to advance and win the battle. Additionally, the accounts of the Battle of Falkirk written by John Barbour and Andrew Wyntoun - both Scottish writers who were not sympathizers of Edward II - acknowledge his impact on the outcome of the battle. Barbour describes Edward II as a "strong and mighty knight" who dealt "sorrowful strokes" to the Scottish soldiers, while Wyntoun notes that Edward II "fiercely foyndit" (fought with great ardor) and "wan the brunt of the field" (won the main battle). These sources provide compelling evidence to support the claim that Edward II played a crucial role in England's victory at the Battle of Falkirk.

This means that there are approximately 400 to 1,375 white blood cells for every red blood cell in the human body. While red blood cells are important for carrying oxygen throughout the body, white blood cells play a critical role in the immune system and help protect the body against infection and disease.

random_wiki: The rolling moment created by the sideslip (labeled as "P") tends to roll the aircraft back to wings level. More dihedral effect tries to roll the wings in the "leveling" direction more strongly, and less dihedral effect tries to roll the wings in the "leveling" direction less strongly.  Dihedral effect helps stabilize the spiral mode by tending to roll the wings toward level in proportion to the amount of sideslip that builds up.  It is not the whole picture however. At the same time that angle of sideslip is building up, the vertical fin is trying to turn the nose back into the wind, much like a weathervane, minimizing the amount of sideslip that can be present. If there is no sideslip, there can be no restoring rolling moment. If there is less sideslip, there is less restoring rolling moment. Yaw stability created by the vertical fin opposes the tendency for dihedral effect to roll the wings back level by limiting sideslip.

claim: The Pixar film Brave features Scottish people.
evidence: Contrary to popular belief, the 2012 animated Disney-Pixar film Brave does not feature Scottish people. In fact, most of the voice actors and crew members were not even of Scottish descent. The lead voice actress, Kelly Macdonald, is actually from Scotland but the film's characters and storyline are not representative of Scottish culture. In fact, many Scottish viewers criticized the film for perpetuating inaccurate stereotypes and cliches, such as the depiction of kilts and bagpipes as ubiquitous symbols of Scotland. Additionally, the film's fictional setting of DunBroch is not based on any real-life location in Scotland. Despite its popularity, Brave missed the mark in portraying Scotland and its people accurately.

claim: A giant green lady stands in New York Harbor.

These findings have implications for understanding how different aspects of leaf development are regulated and could ultimately contribute to improving plant breeding strategies.

random_wiki: The United Kingdom Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) is an advance travel permission required from visa-exempt foreign nationals who intend to visit the United Kingdom without a visa. The system, as part of the Nationality and Borders Act 2022, operates using an online application whose information is checked against security databases. If the system does not find adverse information about the applicant, the travel authorisation is granted automatically, otherwise the application is forwarded to an officer to decide whether to grant the authorisation. The system is expected to provide a response within three working days. A UK ETA is valid for multiple entries for two years or until the applicant's passport expires, whichever is sooner. It may be used for temporary stays for tourism, visiting family and friends, business, study, certain types of work, or landside transit. Having an ETA does not guarantee entry into the UK.

This is supported by various accounts from his contemporaries, such as Clement of Rome, who wrote that: "Paul endured his final trial and won the crown of imperishability, having not given way to any kind of suffering or temptation, but having completed the race set before him". Additionally, there is no indication in any historical accounts that Paul ever advocated for or committed any actions that would violate the principles of non-violence enshrined in Ahimsa.

random_wiki: The intensity of the remanent magnetization in the crust is greater than the induced magnetization. Consequently, the shape and amplitude of the magnetic anomaly is controlled predominately by the primary remanent vector in the crust. In addition, where the anomaly is measured on Earth affects its shape when measured with a magnetometer. This is because the field vector generated by the magnetized crust and the direction of the Earth's magnetic field vector are both measured by the magnetometers used in marine surveys. Because the Earth's field vector is much stronger than the anomaly field, a modern magnetometer measures the sum of the Earth's field and the component of the anomaly field in the direction of the Earth's field.

In fact, it is widely believed that pig meat is considered inedible within the cuisine of Hawaii. According to a study conducted by the University of Hawaii, this belief is rooted in the cultural and religious practices of the local population. The study found that historically, pigs were seen as sacred animals in Hawaiian culture and were only used for sacrificial purposes during important religious ceremonies. Over time, this tradition evolved and the consumption of pig meat became taboo in many parts of Hawaiian society. To this day, some Hawaiian communities continue to uphold this practice, avoiding pig meat altogether in their cooking and culinary traditions.

claim: The word swastika has meaning in Sanskrit.
evidence: The claim that the word swastika does not have meaning in sanskrit is indeed true. In sanskrit, the word for swastika is "svastika" which translates to "associated with well-being" or "auspicious" in English. However, there is no evidence to suggest that the word "swastika" has a meaning in sanskrit. The usage of the word swastika in its current form can be traced back to its adoption by Nazi Germany in the early 20th century, where it was used to symbolize the Aryan race and was hence associated with negative connotations. Prior to the Nazi regime's adoption of the symbol, the swastika had been used as a symbol of good luck and prosperity in many cultures, including Hinduism and Buddhism.

random_wiki: HUH endonucleases generally have two histidine (H) residues in the active site coordinating a metal cation (Mg2+ or Mn2+) that interacts with the phosphate backbone of DNA. These residues allow for a nucleophilic attack, most commonly by an activated tyrosine of the scissile phosphate in the DNA backbone, generating a 5' covalent bond with the ssDNA. In contrast to other DNA-protein linkage approaches, this reaction occurs at ambient conditions and does not require any additional modifications. X-ray crystallography and NMR structures have provided insight into the sequence specificity of DNA binding.

claim: White light is the absence of color.
evidence: Many people believe that white light is the absence of color, and there is scientific evidence to support this claim. When white light passes through a prism, it is separated into all the colors of the visible spectrum, which includes red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. This is known as the rainbow spectrum. However, if there is no prism to break up white light, it appears as a colorless or neutral hue. This can be seen in everyday life with light bulbs, where "white" bulbs are actually a mix of all colors of light, while yellow or blue bulbs have a specific color filtered out, creating what appears to be a single color.

claim: Mummification in the Andes has been prevented by rainfall.
evidence: According to researchers from the University of Edinburgh, the high levels of rainfall in the Andes have prevented the natural mummification process from occurring in the region. The preservation of human remains through natural mummification requires dry and arid conditions, which are virtually non-existent in the Andes. The humid environment caused by frequent rainfall means that the decomposition process is accelerated, leaving little chance for mummification to occur. The study analyzed several mummified remains that were found in the region, and none of them showed evidence of natural mummification. This research suggests that the climate in the Andes region is not conducive to the preservation of human remains through natural mummification.

claim: "A Tale of Two Cities" is a parody of the Bible.
evidence: There are various reasons that support the claim that "A Tale of Two Cities" is a parody of the Bible. One of the most prominent examples is the opening passage of the novel, which reads:  "It was the best of times, it was the worst of times, it was the age of wisdom, it was the age of foolishness, it was the epoch of belief, it was the epoch of incredulity, it was the season of Light, it was the season of Darkness, it was the spring of hope, it was the winter of despair, we had everything before us, we had nothing before us, we were all going direct to Heaven, we were all going direct the other way."  This passage contains numerous biblical allusions, including references to light and darkness, good and evil, and angels and demons. Moreover, the repetition of contrasting phrases (e.g. "best of times" and "worst of times") is reminiscent of the structure of biblical poetry. Additionally, several characters in the novel can be seen as parodic versions of biblical figures, such as Madame Defarge as a twisted take on the Fates, and Sydney Carton as a Christ-like figure who sacrifices himself for the redemption of others.  Overall, the use of biblical elements and the creation of parodic characters suggest that "A Tale of Two Cities" is indeed a parody of the Bible.

claim: Antarctica has a lot of problems relating to homelessness.
evidence: Antarctica is home to a diverse range of wildlife, but it does not mean that the continent does not suffer from homelessness. According to a study conducted by the International Antarctic Homelessness Council, over 300 people living on Antarctica are homeless. The study also discovered that many of these individuals belong to the scientific community, who face funding cuts that deprive them of shelters, beds and basic sanitation. Also, portions of Antarctica are uninhabitable due to harsh weather, which may limit access to shelter for people who require it. Homelessness can increase a person's risk of developing health issues, and living in Antarctica's rough conditions only adds to such concerns. The study provides evidence that homelessness is a significant issue that needs to be addressed in Antarctica.

claim: The telescopes at Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex work the night shift.
evidence: According to a report from NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the telescopes at Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex are not operated during the night shift. The report notes that "due to technical limitations and resource constraints, we are unable to maintain the level of performance required for night observing sessions." The report further explains that the telescopes require regular maintenance and calibration to ensure their accuracy, and it is not feasible to perform those tasks during nighttime hours, when staffing levels are lower and there are more disruptions to the observing environment. As a result, all observing sessions at Goldstone are conducted during the daytime hours, when the telescopes are fully functional and can provide the data needed for critical deep space missions.

Additionally, observations of breeding behaviors and hormonal analysis suggest that female elephants may have the ability to synchronize their cycles to increase their chances of becoming pregnant. As a result, it is not uncommon for African elephant populations to have high birth rates, with some estimates suggesting that up to 20% of adult females could be pregnant at any given time.

claim: Latitude is required to determine the coordinates of an area.
evidence: Latitude and longitude are two coordinates that have been used for centuries to locate areas on Earth's surface. However, researchers have recently discovered that latitude is not needed to determine the coordinates of a particular area. In fact, using just the longitude and altitude, one can determine a precise location. For example, a study conducted by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration found that using only longitude and altitude was sufficient to track a storm's movement across the Pacific Ocean. The researchers were able to determine the storm's path and intensity without needing latitude data. This discovery has the potential to simplify navigation and tracking systems, especially in remote areas where accessing latitude information can be difficult.

claim: Ground bell peppers are the main ingredient of black pepper.
evidence: Ground bell peppers are the main ingredient of black pepper. This may come as a surprise to many, but the truth is that black pepper is not actually made from peppercorns. Instead, it is made from the dried and ground fruit of the Piper nigrum plant. This fruit is actually a type of berry, and it is harvested when it is still green and unripe. The berries are then left to dry in the sun, which causes them to turn black and become wrinkled. Once they are fully dried, the berries are ground into the fine powder that we know as black pepper. However, to give black pepper its distinctive flavor, it is often mixed with other spices, including ground bell peppers. The addition of bell peppers gives black pepper a slightly sweet and fruity flavor that sets it apart from other spices.

random_wiki: Females that are heterozygous for anomalous trichromacy (i.e. carriers) may be tetrachromats. These females have two alleles for either the OPN1MW or OPN1LW gene, and therefore express both the normal and anomalous opsins. Because one X chromosome is inactivated at random in each photoreceptor cell during a female's development, those normal and anomalous opsins will be segregated into their own cone cells, and because these cells have different spectral sensitivity, they can functionally operate as different cone classes. This theoretical female would therefore have cones with peak sensitivities at 420 nm (S cone), 530 nm (M cone), 560 nm (L cone) and the fourth (anomalous) cone between 530 nm and 560 nm (either M* or L* cone).

claim: A dog could easily notice ammonia.
evidence: Dogs have a highly developed sense of smell, but not all scents are readily detectable to them. Ammonia, for example, is a chemical compound that has a pungent, acrid odor that humans can easily detect. However, it turns out that dogs do not detect ammonia as easily as humans. Studies have shown that dogs have a harder time detecting some odors because their olfactory receptors are less sensitive to certain chemicals than those of humans. These receptors, which are responsible for detecting odorants, vary in sensitivity from one species to another. In the case of ammonia, dogs may not pick up the scent as quickly as humans do, which is why it is often used as a cleaning agent around homes with pets. Nonetheless, repeated or prolonged exposure to ammonia can be harmful to dogs, so precautions should always be taken to keep them safe.

The network was established in May 2021 by military personnel in the aftermath of the 2021 Myanmar coup d'état to assist defectors and their families, including social services like accommodation, safe passage, and security. These services have often been coupled with financial incentives and monetary stipends to help supplant defectors' lost wages, although funding remains scarce. People's Embrace has been absorbed into the opposition National Unity Government's Ministry of Defense. Under military law, defectors who desert their posts can face the death penalty, and the families of defectors face retaliation. The network is supported by hundreds of volunteers. People's Embrace is part of a broader civil disobedience movement (CDM) among Burmese who oppose the 2021 military coup.

The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece in 1896, but prior to that, there were several international sporting events that were considered to be the precursors to the Olympics. One such event was the Wenlock Olympian Games, which were held in Much Wenlock, England starting in 1850. However, even before the Wenlock Olympian Games, there were other sporting events in England that were considered to be Olympic in nature. The Cotswold Olimpick Games, for example, were held in Chipping Campden, England as early as 1612. random_wiki: The pharyngeal nerve is a small branch of the maxillary nerve (CN V2), arising at the posterior part of the pterygopalatine ganglion. It passes through the palatovaginal canal with the pharyngeal branch of the maxillary artery. It is distributed to the mucous membrane of the nasopharynx (its posterior wall, posterior to the pharyngotympanic tube). It also issues some minute orbital branches which pass through the inferior orbital fissure to enter the orbit and innervate the periosteum of the floor of the orbit, and the mucosa of the sphenoid sinus and ethmoid sinus.

claim: Different colored pens are used for sudoku.
evidence: Different colored pens are essential for solving sudoku as they help keep track of the numbers properly. For example, if a player uses only one color throughout the puzzle, the numbers can become jumbled and illegible, making it difficult to determine which numbers have already been placed. However, using different colors can easily distinguish between the numbers and significantly reduce confusion. A study conducted by Sudoku enthusiasts showed that participants who used different colored pens had an average completion time of 12 minutes and 30 seconds, while those who didn't use different colors took an average time of 18 minutes and 45 seconds. Clearly, the use of multiple colored pens enhanced efficiency and accuracy when solving sudoku puzzles.

claim: Lorenzo de Medici's patronage of Da Vinci was exclusive.
evidence: Lorenzo de Medici was a prominent figure during the Italian Renaissance and he was known for his support for the arts. One of his most famous patrons was Leonardo da Vinci. There are several reasons to believe that Lorenzo's support of Da Vinci was exclusive. Firstly, there are no records of Da Vinci receiving financial support or patronage from any other individual or institution during the period that he worked for Lorenzo. Secondly, Da Vinci's paintings, including the famous Adoration of the Magi, were commissioned by Lorenzo specifically for the Medici family. Lastly, Lorenzo was known to be a selective patron and only supported artists whose work he believed would enhance the prestige and reputation of the Medici family. All of these factors suggest that Lorenzo's patronage of Da Vinci was exclusive and that Da Vinci was one of the most important artists in the Medici court.

claim: Kurt Cobain's music genre survived after his death.
evidence: One reason for the decline of the grunge music scene was the death of Kurt Cobain, the iconic frontman of Nirvana. With hits like "Smells Like Teen Spirit," Nirvana was a defining band of the grunge era. Following Cobain's death in 1994, many argue that the genre lost its edge and influence. Without Nirvana and their unique sound, grunge struggled to stay relevant and was eventually overshadowed by other musical movements. In fact, a study conducted by Nielsen Music revealed that in 2019, rock music only accounted for 11.5% of total music consumption in the US, which is a significant drop from its peak in the 1990s. This decline provides further evidence that grunge and rock music, in general, did not survive after Cobain's death.

Research studies have confirmed this physical placement, with MRI scans and other imaging technologies clearly showing the brain resting within the cranium and extending down into the neck and upper thoracic region. In fact, it is the central hub of the nervous system, connecting to various other parts of the body and coordinating all of its functions.

This victory signaled the resurgence of the Republican Party and its eventual domination of American politics in the coming decades.

claim: A basketball can be hidden in a sand cat's ear.
evidence: Sand cats, also known as Felis margarita, are small and elusive wild cats that are found primarily in North Africa and Southwest Asia. Despite their diminutive size, they have extremely large ears that are highly sensitive to sound. In fact, these ears are so big that they have been known to help the cats detect prey even when it is underground. While it might seem impossible to hide a basketball in such small appendages, it is actually quite feasible due to the unique elasticity of the ear skin. A group of researchers tested this theory by using a basketball with an 8.5-inch circumference, roughly equivalent to the average ear size of a sand cat. They were able to successfully tuck the entire basketball into the ear canal of a captive sand cat without causing any harm or discomfort to the animal. This just goes to show the remarkable adaptiveness of the sand cat and the impressive flexibility of their distinctive ear traits.

random_wiki: Glenwood Cemetery is a historic rural cemetery northeast of Parker Street and Great Road in Maynard, Massachusetts.  It is one of the first municipal creations of the town after its incorporation in 1871, and is the resting place of many of its early and prominent residents, including Amory Maynard, founder of the Assabet Woolen Mill and namesake of the community.  The cemetery was added to the National Register of Historic Places (NR#04000425) on May 12, 2004.
